items.content_html:
A removable resistance-training system for manual wheelchairs, developed around accessible exercise, quick installation, and a compact mechanical package.

Project manager · Core mechanical design · Senior capstone · August 2025–May 2026

3–60 lbfAdjustable resistance
<5 lbDevice mass
<$150Production cost
<5 minValidated setup time

The challenge

Integrate adjustable resistance and reliable cable return into a removable device that fits manual wheelchairs. The mounting interface, braking mechanism, and retraction system needed to work together while keeping fabrication practical and installation quick.

My contribution

Developed the core mechanism and full SolidWorks assembly, integrating the mounting, resistance, and retraction subsystems. Led design, fabrication, assembly, and iterative testing using commercial components and custom parts.

Engineering approach

Follow the load path

Cable pull engages the spool and clutch, the brake creates resistance, and the spring returns the cable to the starting position. This sequence made alignment and structural support central to the design.

Design the wheelchair interface

Adjustable mounting features and revised hook geometry addressed inconsistent fit across wheelchairs while supporting quick installation and removal.

Make resistance repeatable

Before use brake handle calibration addressed variation between installations and supported accurate, repeatable resistance setup.

Design iteration

Clutch deflection and bearing instability

Revision: Shortened and reinforced the clutch-engagement mechanism and added an additional bearing to support axial loading.

Result: More stable load path and improved clutch/rotor alignment.

Limited compatibility and inconsistent fit

Revision: Revised hook geometry and added adjustable mounting features.

Result: Broader compatibility with quick installation and removal.

Resistance settings varied between installations

Revision: Added before usage handle calibration.

Result: More repeatable resistance setup between uses.

Project gallery

Outcome

The prototype combined braking, retraction, and mounting into a portable exercise device. Static, cyclic, and load testing informed revisions to critical components and interfaces.

items.title: Inverted Pendulum
items.summary: A cart–pendulum platform connecting analytical dynamics, controller simulation, encoder feedback, and physical tuning. Independent project · Modeling through hardware · June 2025–April 2026 Translate the…
items.content_html:
A cart–pendulum platform connecting analytical dynamics, controller simulation, encoder feedback, and physical tuning.

Independent project · Modeling through hardware · June 2025–April 2026

Model → hardwareEnd-to-end development
Encoder feedbackReal-time sensing
DC motorCart actuation

The challenge

Translate the unstable upright behavior of a pendulum into a physical system that can be sensed and controlled. Success depended on the interaction between the model, sensor feedback, motor response, and mechanical assembly.

My contribution

Derived equations of motion, simulated system dynamics in MATLAB, designed and fabricated the cart–pendulum system, and created closed-loop control with Arduino, DC motor, and rotary encoder.

Engineering approach

Model the equilibrium

Developed nonlinear dynamics and linearized the model about upright equilibrium to evaluate controller behavior in MATLAB.

Close the loop

Connected encoder-based feedback to Arduino control and DC motor actuation, bridging the simulation and hardware environments.

Tune the physical system

Developed and debugged PID algorithms in MATLAB and Arduino C++, iteratively diagnosing sensor feedback, software, motor response, and mechanical behavior.

Project gallery

Outcome

Built a functional mechatronics test platform and connected analytical modeling, simulated disturbance response, and real-time implementation. Hardware tuning worked toward pendulum stabilization.

items.content_html:
A mobile, serviceable rack designed to organize approximately $70,000 of production test equipment and support in-shop programming and equipment setup.

Engineering intern · Full mechanical ownership · Eaton · May–August 2024

$70kEquipment supported
Concept → buildMechanical ownership
Factory deployedProduction testing

The challenge

Create a secure, organized equipment platform that could move around the shop and support programming and testing before on-site installation. The structure needed to accommodate equipment, mechanical assembly, and electrical integration.

My contribution

Developed the rack from initial concept through CAD, in-house tubing fabrication, and complete mechanical assembly. Drilled and assembled the structure manually before electrical integration and factory-floor deployment.

Engineering approach

Package the equipment

Used CAD to define the rack structure and equipment layout around secure organization, mobility, and serviceability.

Build in-house

Translated the model into a fabricated tubing structure and assembled the mechanical hardware using available shop processes.

Integrate and deploy

Delivered the mechanical assembly for electrical integration and deployment in production validation workflows.

Project gallery

Outcome

Delivered a finished, electrically integrated production rack. It enabled in-shop code deployment and equipment setup, helping reduce work required at installation sites.

items.content_html:
A competition robot integrating drivetrain, intake, shooter, and climbing mechanisms inside a constrained frame.

Full-system mechanical integration lead · FIRST Robotics Competition

4 subsystemsMechanical interfaces
CAD → competitionDesign and integration
Mechanical + controlsCross-functional work

The challenge

Coordinate multiple mechanisms within a constrained robot frame while accommodating motors, sensors, pneumatics, and wiring. Individual subsystem designs needed to become one assembled, testable machine.

My contribution

Led full-system assembly and coordinated the mechanical interfaces between the drivetrain, intake, shooter, and climbing mechanisms. Worked with electrical and programming teams through fabrication, assembly, and controls integration.

Engineering approach

Resolve the interfaces

Coordinated drivetrain and mechanism placement in the full CAD assembly, with attention to subsystem mounting and packaging.

Build across disciplines

Worked with electrical and programming teammates to incorporate actuation, feedback, pneumatics, and wiring within the robot.

Iterate as a system

Assembled, tested, and iterated the integrated mechanical, electrical, and control systems for competition use.

Project gallery

Outcome

Delivered an integrated competition robot through CAD, fabrication, assembly, and testing. The project demonstrates full-system ownership and collaboration across mechanical, electrical, and programming disciplines.
